routes.label: Add work rates and use the formula
Use Gamma's share of the combined rate

question: Three men, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma, working together, do a job in \(6\) hours less time than Alpha alone, in \(1\) hour less time than Beta alone, and in one-half the time needed by Gamma when working alone. Let \(h\) be the number of hours needed by Alpha and Beta, working together, to do the job. Then \(h\) equals:
solution:
Gamma alone takes twice as long as all three together, so Gamma supplies half their combined work rate. Alpha and Beta must supply the other half.

Let \(t>0\) be the number of hours needed by all three together, and take the whole job as one unit of work. Their individual completion times are \(t+6\), \(t+1\), and \(2t\). Thus Gamma's rate is \(1/(2t)\) job per hour, while the combined rate is \(1/t\). Alpha and Beta's combined rate is therefore also \(1/(2t)\), giving
\[
\frac1{t+6}+\frac1{t+1}=\frac1{2t}.
\]
All denominators are positive. Multiplying by \(2t(t+6)(t+1)\) gives
\[
2t(2t+7)=(t+6)(t+1).
\]
Expanding and factoring,
\[
3t^2+7t-6=(3t-2)(t+3)=0.
\]
The root \(-3\) is inadmissible because \(t>0\), leaving \(t=2/3\).

Since Alpha and Beta's combined rate is \(1/(2t)\), their completion time is
\[
\boxed{h=2t=\frac43\text{ hours}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{C}\).
